public_rationale: On 2026-03-23, Reuters reported, citing sources, that the private equity investment in OpenAI's joint venture included seniority over other joint venture partners and downside protection. Those terms appeared under a section headed 'sweeteners'. On 2026-05-04, The Next Web, citing Yahoo Finance and Reuters, reported that the venture had been finalised and that OpenAI was guaranteeing its private equity backers a 17.5% annual return over five years. On 2026-02-27, Tom's Hardware reported that $35 billion of Amazon's $50 billion commitment was contingent on conditions that may require an IPO or an 'AGI milestone', according to sources cited by The Information. All of these reports came before the 2026-06-10 post. They show OpenAI agreeing to unusual investor-friendly terms in 2026, which meets the support condition. The 'more and more' trend rests on how new these terms were, not on a measured comparison with earlier rounds.
limitations: The deal terms come from reporting that cites unnamed sources or relays other outlets. The contracts are not public.
The seniority, downside protection and 17.5% guarantee apply to the joint venture, not to OpenAI's main equity round.
The Amazon conditions are reported as ones that 'may' require an IPO or an AGI milestone. Their exact terms are not confirmed.
The increase implied by 'more and more' was not measured against OpenAI's earlier rounds.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: in its recent fundraising, OpenAI has been agreeing to terms that favor investors (contingent tranches, guaranteed returns, seniority, downside protection) beyond ordinary equity terms.
No period was named. I read it as describing OpenAI's 2026 fundraising up to the post date (January 2026 to 2026-06-10), which covers the deals he mentions.
'More and more' is read loosely: a run of new, unusually investor-friendly terms in recent deals. A strict measured increase compared with every earlier round is not required.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reports from early-to-mid 2026 show OpenAI giving investors unusual protective or sweetened terms, such as contingent tranches or guaranteed minimum returns.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible reports show that OpenAI's recent deals used plain equity terms without special investor protections, or that the reported sweeteners never existed or were withdrawn.
